content:
The test image shows a microscopic view of soybean stem tissue with numerous small black specks (microsclerotia) scattered throughout pale/cream-colored tissue — the classic "charcoal-sprinkled" appearance. The specks are randomly distributed (not in linear rows, which would indicate Diaporthe).

The Charcoal Rot reference confirms: split stems with pale internal tissue dotted with black microsclerotia matches exactly.

{"prediction": "Charcoal_Rot", "confidence": 0.88, "reasoning": "Microscopic close-up of stem tissue showing numerous small black specks (microsclerotia) scattered throughout pale cream-colored pith/vascular tissue. This is the characteristic 'charcoal-sprinkled' appearance of Charcoal Rot caused by Macrophomina phaseolina. The random distribution of specks rules out Diaporthe (which shows linear rows of pycnidia), and the stem-internal context rules out foliar diseases."}
